items.title: 'I thought I was going to die' - Venezuelans describe earthquake panic
items.description: Buildings were flattened in the capital Caracas, where voices have been heard calling from the rubble.

items.title: France, UK and Spain see record temperatures as heatwave grips western Europe
items.description: Tens of millions of people are grappling with punishing temperatures, which have led to red heat alerts across the continent.

items.title: Trump asks Congress for billions for Iran war, after tension with Republicans
items.description: But the budget faces an uphill battle as the president spars with some members of his own party over the issue.

items.title: Oil price falls to levels not seen since before Iran war
items.description: Energy prices have been on a wild ride since Iran responded to US and Israeli attacks by effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Philippines bans video game played by alleged high school shooter
items.description: The rare school shooting that left three students killed and 20 others injured has shocked the country.

items.title: Police seal off key roads in Nairobi as Kenya braces for Gen Z protests
items.description: Protesters demand justice for more than 80 people killed during the 2024 demonstrations and last year's anniversary protests.

items.description: The firm alleged that Alibaba used fraudulent accounts to access data from its Claude AI model.

items.title: Independent MPs launch new Australian centrist party
items.description: Zali Steggall and Allegra Spender say Community Strong Australia will offer citizens 'reason over rage'.

items.title: Air conditioning creates political divide after France records hottest day
items.description: France is being forced to re-think its longstanding reservations about air-conditioning as temperatures soar.

items.title: Biggest city in Crimea without power after Ukraine strikes
items.description: Sevastopol's Moscow-installed governor warns there will be no electricity in some areas until the evening.

items.title: UN nuclear chief says inspectors will visit Iran sites as part of war deal
items.description: Rafael Grossi says the IAEA is "working on modalities" but an Iranian  minister says such access would only be part of a final deal with the US.
